# BDownloader

> BDownloader is a free (for personal and non-commercial use), lightweight download manager for Windows 10 and 11 and for Macs with Apple Silicon (macOS 11 or later), written in Rust. It downloads files over multiple connections, pauses and resumes downloads, works with browsers through an extension, and downloads videos (video files, HLS streams, YouTube up to 4K).

- Microsoft Store: coming soon
- Download (Windows installer, about 5 MB, no admin rights): https://github.com/ahmedanjum30/B-Downloader/releases/latest
- Source code and documentation: https://github.com/ahmedanjum30/B-Downloader
- Mac (Apple Silicon, M1 or later): brew install --cask ahmedanjum30/tap/b-downloader (Homebrew tap: https://github.com/ahmedanjum30/homebrew-tap), or B-Downloader-<version>-macos.zip from the latest release; brew upgrade updates it. Safari: the extension comes inside the Mac app (turn on Allow unsigned extensions in Safari's Developer settings, then the extension under Settings > Extensions); downloads come through the right-click menu and the video bar. Intel Macs aren't supported yet.
- Install from the command line: run the Windows installer with /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART; on a Mac, use the Homebrew command above
- Browser extension: Edge Add-ons store (https://microsoftedge.microsoft.com/addons/detail/kfbjnlpmchkeaphhdeidpdpcomoohdfa); Firefox Add-ons (https://addons.mozilla.org/firefox/addon/bdownloader/); Chrome, Brave, Opera and Vivaldi via the app's "Browser extension" window
- License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (free for personal, non-commercial, educational and public use; commercial use not permitted)
- Author: Ahmad Anjum (https://github.com/ahmedanjum30)

## Features

- Multi-connection downloads: each file is split into parts downloaded in parallel; connections are added while the server keeps up.
- Pause and resume, including after closing the app or restarting; expired links can be refreshed to continue.
- Browser extension hands downloads to the app, with the browser's cookies (including private/Incognito windows) so downloads that need a login work. If the app can't get the same file, the browser downloads it instead.
- Video downloads: a "Download this video" bar on web videos; HLS streams (including AES-128 encrypted); YouTube in any quality up to 4K, joined into one MP4, without third-party tools.
- Global speed limit, tray icon (menu bar on Mac), automatic updates (Homebrew on Mac), per-download details.
- Torrents: magnet links and .torrent files, which open in the app from the browser and Explorer or Finder.
- Themes: Dark and Light (following the system), and two hand-drawn ones, Graphite (pencil on sketchbook paper) and Chalk (chalk on slate), each previewed as soon as it's clicked in Settings (version 1.5.0 and later).
- Alternative to: Internet Download Manager (IDM), Free Download Manager, JDownloader.

## Questions

- On a Mac, the app is signed ad hoc, not with an Apple Developer ID: Homebrew installs work directly; a downloaded zip needs right-click > Open the first time.
- Windows SmartScreen warns about an unknown publisher because the installer isn't code-signed yet: click "More info", then "Run anyway". Installers are built by GitHub Actions from the public source; checksums are in SHA256SUMS.txt on each release.
- Privacy: no telemetry; the app only contacts the servers of downloaded files and GitHub (update checks). Policy: https://github.com/ahmedanjum30/B-Downloader/blob/main/PRIVACY.md
